entries.title: Tutorial
entries.content:
This is the tutorial, designed to help you find your way around the app. Before the performance begins, you can reopen it at any time via the information icon in the top left.

You will also find the button to change the language there.

entries.title: Do Not Disturb
entries.content: Set your phone to 'Do Not Disturb'.

entries.title: Vesalius
entries.content:
If you click on the information icon in the top left, you can find some background information. This will change for each part of the performance.

The information was compiled by Dr. Thomas Moors.

entries.title: Performance
entries.content:
Mathias Coppens' composition takes the work of Vesalius as a guide.

This music is accompanied by live visuals by Klaas Verpoest and Jan Duerinck. Each part is preceded by an introductory video from Complete Anatomy.

entries.title: Performance
entries.content:
The life of Vesalius is given voice in the 'architecture sonore' by Mireille Capelle. The sound art is by Bodo Peeters, and the video was created by Ezayona Capelle.

The piece is brought together under the direction of Fleur Khani.

entries.title: Sounds
entries.content:
On the next page, you can experiment with controlling the sounds that will come from your phone at certain moments during the performance, becoming part of the musical whole.

The idea is that you can adjust the sound using sliders. Feel free to experiment!

entries.title: Participation
entries.content:
At certain moments during the performance, a group of people will be given the chance to come forward, chosen at random.

It will then be explained what is expected at that moment. These are always very simple actions.

entries.title: Effects
entries.content:
Furthermore, your phone will occasionally do something—for example, visually—and sometimes your phone will even vibrate.

If you don't see sliders to manipulate the sound or don't receive a message, you don't need to interact with your phone, but you will automatically contribute to the atmosphere of the music.

Don't forget to set your phone's volume to maximum.
